research: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/speech-generation: official voice list with one-word characters (Puck Upbeat, Enceladus Breathy, Iapetus Clear, Umbriel Easy-going, Algieba Smooth, Achird Friendly, Zubenelgenubi Casual, Sadachbia Lively); long director's-note blocks cause drift, keep notes short; pace via plain words like 'speaking rapidly'; the voice choice carries permanent traits
https://docs.cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/docs/gemini-tts: all eight allowed voices are listed as male

https://dev.to/googleai/how-to-prompt-gemini-31s-new-text-to-speech-model-24bb: Google's 3.1 TTS prompting guide; name a specific place (e.g. Croydon) rather than 'British accent'; regions like London/Newcastle/Exeter give distinct results
https://livekit.com/blog/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-prompting-guide: accent is treated as a style instruction; don't overspecify; keep style, script and tags pointing the same way

https://www.famulor.io/blog/gemini-31-flash-tts-prompting-guide-for-ai-voice-agents: words like 'quiet' or 'flat' in notes make output monotone; describe the situation and listener instead of adjectives; never quote transcript words inside the notes or the engine may speak them
https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/is-there-an-update-to-gemini-tts-gemini-went-british/87084: British accent can be intermittent; guide it through the prompt

options.idea: Mid-forties Birmingham lifer, twenty years on the road; the breathy, lived-in voice suits a tired, solid man whose calm finally cracks.
options.note:
Accent: ordinary working-class Birmingham, light and everyday, the way he actually talks, never put on.
Style: experienced paramedic in his forties, crouched over a dying man, reporting to his colleague; then, stunned, to the driver up front.
Pace: quick, clipped, then sharp.

options.idea: Late-twenties South Londoner, a couple of years qualified; Puck's bright energy reads as a younger man running on adrenaline and fear.
options.note:
Accent: working-class Croydon, south London, natural and understated, not a caricature.
Style: young paramedic, late twenties, scared but holding it together, calling numbers to his senior colleague, then shouting forward in disbelief at the driver.
Pace: fast, breathless, rising.

options.idea: Mid-thirties Leeds paramedic, lower-middle class, ex-army steadiness; Algieba's smooth, even voice gives a controlled man whose control snaps.
options.note:
Accent: lower-middle-class Leeds, Yorkshire, soft and everyday, nothing theatrical.
Style: steady paramedic in his mid-thirties, ex-forces, giving his colleague the readings plainly; then genuinely thrown, asking the driver what's happening.
Pace: brisk and firm, then urgent.

notes: Notes avoid quoting the lines (engine can speak them) and avoid 'flat/quiet' words. All three are male voices from the allowed list; they differ on age (20s/30s/40s), region (Birmingham/Croydon/Leeds), class and temperament.
